claims.claim: Python's built-in numeric types include integers, floating-point numbers, and complex numbers.
Python integers have arbitrary precision, subject to practical memory limits.
A complex number has real and imaginary components, written with a j suffix in Python literals such as 1+2j.
Most decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly as binary floating-point fractions, so a displayed or computed float can contain a small representation error.
Python's round() rounds ties to the nearest even multiple and can produce results that surprise users when the input is a float such as 2.675.
For integers a//b is floor division and a%b has a result consistent with a == (a//b)*b + (a%b).
